commit 9e881ab9b8bc9cca3175fd5354131cd9167d5892
Author: Matthias Wenz <matthias@entire.io>
Date:   Wed Sep 9 12:28:05 2026 +0200

    refactor: render the auth context picker as the contexts table
    
    The picker listed each context as "name · handle · server", which showed
    the same fields as `entire auth contexts` in a different shape. It now
    uses that command's aligned CONTEXT / HANDLE / LOGIN SERVER columns.
    
    Options are single-line strings in huh, so the header cannot be one of
    them — it would be selectable. It goes in the field description instead,
    indented by the width of the select cursor so the columns sit above the
    option text rather than above the cursor. Header and rows come from one
    width calculation, so they cannot drift apart.
    
    The active context keeps its trailing "(active)" rather than the table's
    leading "*". huh draws its cursor in that leading column and the cursor
    moves, while "(active)" says which context is in use; putting both in
    one column would make the row you happen to be sitting on read as the
    current one.
    
    Three consolidations rather than new copies:
    
    - alignTableLines is split out of renderAlignedTable, which now calls
      it. The picker needs the columns as strings, not written to a writer,
      so both share one gutter/width implementation. It trims trailing
      padding, which matters here: huh styles the whole label, so padding
      would widen the selected row's highlight past its text.
    - The indent is uiform.SelectOptionIndent, defined beside the theme that
      sets the selector. TestSelectOptionIndentMatchesSelector asserts it
      equals the real selector width in both light and dark, so a change to
      the cursor string fails a test instead of quietly misaligning the
      header.
    - unparam flagged fallback(s, alt) once every caller passed the same
      placeholder. Collapsing it surfaced an identical orDash already in
      repo_mirror.go, same package, so there is now one instead of three.
      The surviving version trims whitespace — a cell of spaces looks empty
      but breaks alignment.
    
    Labels carry no styling of their own; huh colors the selected row, and
    an embedded color would fight it.
    
    In ACCESSIBLE=1 huh does not render field descriptions, so the header
    line is absent there. The columns still align with each other and
    "(active)" still shows.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M22VBSK5P5XNRFQFATXZASJJ

content.text:
## What the last commit (`9e881ab9b`) is for

The previous commit added the interactive picker to `entire auth use`, and rendered each context as `name · handle · server`. That's the same three fields `entire auth contexts` prints, in a second, ad-hoc shape. The last commit is a pure presentation refactor: **make the picker render as the same aligned `CONTEXT / HANDLE / LOGIN SERVER` table the listing command prints**, and do it by sharing code rather than copying it.

Concretely:

- `alignTableLines` is extracted from `renderAlignedTable` (`auth.go:585`) so the picker can get the columns as *strings* — huh needs each row as an option label and can't write to a writer. `renderAlignedTable` now just prints those lines.
- Rows become option labels; the header can't be an option (it would be selectable), so it goes in the field description, prefixed by `uiform.SelectOptionIndent` — the width of huh's `"> "` cursor — so the header sits over the option text, not over the cursor. `TestSelectOptionIndentMatchesSelector` pins that constant to the real selector width in both themes.
- The active row keeps a trailing `(active)` instead of the listing's leading `*`, because huh's moving cursor already owns the leading column.
- Two dedup passes fall out: `fallback(s, alt)` (always called with the same placeholder) collapses into `orDash`, which was already duplicated in `repo_mirror.go`; three copies become one.

Rendered result (verified locally):

```
  CONTEXT     HANDLE  LOGIN SERVER
> entire-io   victor  https://core.entire.io
  staging-eu  -       https://core.staging.eu.entire.io  (active)
  local       dev     -
```

## Review

Tests and lint pass (`go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... -run 'Context|AuthUse'`, `golangci-lint v2.11.3`: 0 issues). I traced the huh v2 internals for the assumptions this commit rests on, and they hold:

- `RunAccessible` prints title + `%d. %s` options only — the description really is dropped under `ACCESSIBLE=1`, as claimed.
- `renderOption` indents unselected rows by exactly `lipgloss.Width(SelectSelector)`, so pinning the indent to that width is the right invariant.
- `Options()` → `Value()` ordering is fine: `Accessor()` calls `selectValue(current)` (cursor lands on the active context) then `updateValue()`, so even an empty `current_context` leaves `selected` set to a real option — the `selected == ""` guard is defensive, not load-bearing.
- `orDash`'s new `TrimSpace` is a deliberate, harmless widening for the two `repo_mirror.go` call sites; `placeholderDash` is `"-"`, so their output is unchanged for real values.
- `rowLine`'s `TrimRight` is a no-op for the existing tables (`writeRow` never padded the last cell either), so no listing output changes.

Nothing blocking. Four small things:

1. **The `ACCESSIBLE=1` claim is true only up to 9 contexts.** huh writes `"%d. %s"`, so a 10th row's label starts one column later than the 9th and the columns step. The commit message states flatly that "the columns still align with each other" there. Either qualify it, or accept it — with ten saved logins it's a cosmetic wobble.

2. **Narrow terminals break the header/row alignment asymmetrically.** huh wraps the description at `width - frame` but options at `width - frame - cursorW` (`field_select.go:581` vs `:680`), so a row wraps two cells before the header does. Only bites when the terminal is narrower than the widest row; graceful degradation, worth knowing rather than fixing.

3. **`selectOptionIndent` in `utils.go:30` is an alias with one caller.** `uiform.SelectOptionIndent` used directly in `auth_context.go` would drop the indirection without costing anything.

4. **Test nit:** `columnOffsets` returns rune indices and they're compared against `strings.Index`'s byte offsets. Equal for the ASCII fixtures, but a non-ASCII context name added later would fail confusingly.

On the PR as a whole (`ea3955b25`): the optional-arg picker follows `selectPlacement`, and the non-interactive path errors with every candidate name plus `entire auth use <name>` rather than hanging — which is what the agent-safe-fallback rule in CLAUDE.md asks for. Reading `StoredContexts` rather than `Contexts` is the right call and the reasoning is captured at the call site.

Not byte-identical — same three columns, same alignment engine (`alignTableLines`), but four deliberate differences:

```
--- entire auth contexts ---        --- entire auth use ---
   CONTEXT     HANDLE  LOGIN SERVER   CONTEXT     HANDLE  LOGIN SERVER
   entire-io   victor  https://…      entire-io   victor  https://…
*  staging-eu  -       https://…    > staging-eu  -       https://…  (active)
   local       dev     -              local       dev     -
```

1. **Active marker.** The listing has a leading `*` column; the picker puts `(active)` in a trailing column, because huh's `>` cursor already owns the leading column and it moves as you scroll.
2. **Leading width.** `*` plus the 2-space gutter makes the listing 3 columns deep on the left; huh's cursor is 2 (`"> "`). So the two commands' headers don't start at the same offset — they only align internally, each with its own rows.
3. **Styling.** The listing bolds headers and the active name and colors the `*` via `authTableStyles`; picker labels are deliberately unstyled so huh's selected/unselected option colors don't fight an embedded color.
4. **Context set.** The picker drops nameless entries (not selectable by `SetCurrentContext`); the listing shows whatever is in `contexts.json`.

Plus the framing: the picker adds a title and the description sentence above the header, and under `ACCESSIBLE=1` huh drops the description entirely, so the header line disappears there while the rows stay aligned.

So: same table *shape*, shared width calculation, but the two are not interchangeable renderings.

content.text:
Yes. And there's an argument for it beyond symmetry: `(active)` is already the spelling in shell completion (`auth_context.go:218`), so `*` in the listing is the odd one out of three surfaces.

The change in `renderContextsTable` is small:

```go
header := []string{
    sty.render(sty.header, "CONTEXT"),
    sty.render(sty.header, "HANDLE"),
    sty.render(sty.header, "LOGIN SERVER"),
    "", // active marker
}
...
marker := ""
name := sty.render(sty.value, c.Name)
if c.Name == current {
    marker = sty.render(sty.id, "(active)")
    name = sty.render(sty.name, c.Name)
}
```

That drops the leading column, so the listing becomes exactly the picker's rows (the picker just adds huh's 2-space cursor gutter and skips the bolding). `TestRenderContextsTable` at `auth_context_test.go:184` asserts `*`, so it'd move to `(active)`.

Two things to weigh against it:

- **`*` in a leading column is the convention** for exactly this table — `kubectl config get-contexts`, `git branch`. It's also faster to scan down a long list than a word at a ragged right edge, since the trailing column's start moves with the widest LOGIN SERVER.
- **It changes a shipped command's output**, and this PR's objective is the picker. It's a one-line-ish change, but a separate concern.

My recommendation: do it, in a follow-up commit or PR rather than folded into the picker work — the unification is worth it once completion, picker, and listing all say the same word, but it should be reviewable as "change how `auth contexts` marks the active row", not buried in the picker refactor.

content.text:
It's wrong — the premise is right and both consequences it predicts are false.

**What's true:** `StoredContexts` (`auth/context_store.go:194`) really does return `f.CurrentContext` unvalidated, so `current` can name a context that isn't in `named` (deleted, renamed, hand-edited, or nameless and filtered out by the loop above).

**What's false:** everything it claims follows from that. huh normalizes the value at build time. `Options()` calls `updateValue()`, and `Value()` → `Accessor()` calls `selectValue(get())` then `updateValue()` again (`field_select.go:91-96`, `:176-188`), and `updateValue` writes `filteredOptions[s.selected].Value` back through the pointer. So a stale name is overwritten with a real option before the form ever runs:

```
current=""                -> selected="prod"
current="deleted-context" -> selected="prod"
current="staging"         -> selected="staging"
```

That's the field built exactly as `selectContextToUse` builds it, read before any input. It's not order-fragile either — I tried `Value()` before `Options()` and got the same result, because both call `updateValue()`.

So:

- *"may fail to preselect anything"* — the cursor lands on row 0. There is nothing else it could do; the stale name names no row. Preselecting the context being replaced is a nicety that degrades correctly when there's nothing to preselect.
- *"return an out-of-offer value"* — impossible. The variable holds a real option value before `RunWithContext` is called, and `selectContextToUse` still has the `selected == ""` guard behind that.

Its suggested fix — "pick a safe default from the options, only prefer `current` when it's present in `named`" — is a reimplementation of `selectValue`/`updateValue`. It'd be dead code.

Fair to Copilot: it's a plausible read if you assume `Value(&x)` is a plain binding rather than something that mutates `x` at construction. But it's a static-analysis guess presented as a defect, and it doesn't survive being run.

Want me to reply on the thread with the evidence and resolve it?

  --title "Mark the active context the same way in both context tables" --body-file - <<'EOF'
Stacked on #2326.

`entire auth contexts` flagged the active context with a leading `*` while the `entire auth use` picker (added in #2326) used a trailing `(active)`. Two renderings of the same three columns, disagreeing about where the marker lives and what it says — and shell completion already appends `(active)`, so `*` was the odd one out of the three surfaces.

The listing now follows the picker:

```
$ entire auth contexts                    entire auth use
CONTEXT     HANDLE  LOGIN SERVER            CONTEXT     HANDLE  LOGIN SERVER
entire-io   victor  https://…               entire-io   victor  https://…
staging-eu  -       https://…  (active)   > staging-eu  -       https://…  (active)
local       dev     -                       local       dev     -
```

Identical apart from huh's cursor gutter.

### Why the trailing column

It is what the picker needs: huh draws its cursor in the leading column and the cursor *moves*, so a marker there makes whichever row you are sitting on read as the current one. The listing has no cursor and could keep `*`, but then it stays a second spelling of one fact.

### One table, not two

`contextTableLines` is now the only place these columns are built. Both callers pass an `authTableStyles`, which already renders plain text when color is off, so the picker gets its unstyled rows by passing an unset one rather than keeping its own copy of the column list. `TestContextTableMatchesPicker` compares the two renderings line for line, so a column added to one cannot go missing from the other, and the marker cannot drift back to two spellings.

### Trade-off

Stated because it is real: `*` in a leading column is the convention for this table (`kubectl config get-contexts`, `git branch`) and scans faster down a long list than a word at a ragged right edge, since the marker's start moves with the widest LOGIN SERVER. This is a deliberate choice of consistency across the three surfaces over that convention.

`mise run check` (fmt, lint, unit + integration + Vogon canary) passes.

content.text:
Opened **#2347**, based on `feat/auth-use-interactive-picker` (not `main`), so it stacks on #2326: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2347

What it does:

- `entire auth contexts` drops the leading `*` column for a trailing `(active)`, matching the picker and the `(active)` shell completion already appends. The two tables now render identically apart from huh's cursor gutter.
- `contextTableLines` becomes the single builder for both. The picker gets unstyled rows by passing an unset `authTableStyles` — which already means "render plain text" — instead of keeping its own copy of the column list.
- `TestContextTableMatchesPicker` compares the two renderings line for line, so the marker can't drift back into two spellings and a column can't go missing from one side.
- The `*`-is-conventional trade-off is written into both the commit message and the PR body rather than dropped silently.

`mise run check` passes. One thing worth knowing: the full-package `TestRunUninstall_*` tests failed first time from those stale `entire-agent-*` mise shims again — I deleted the three shim files (`devin`, `kilo`, `roger-roger`) and the suite went green.
